title: The choice a partition forces
description: The network splits. Replica A cannot reach Replica B. A write arrives at A, and A cannot know whether B will serve a stale read. There is no option that is both correct and available.

steps.text: The write reaches Replica A, which cannot confirm that B will learn about it.
Replication is severed. A knows it is isolated.

B refuses the read — or A refuses the write — rather than risk serving data it cannot vouch for. Every answer the system gives is correct; some requests get no answer at all. This is what a ledger or an inventory decrement should do: a rejected transaction is annoying, a double-spend is not.
A accepts the write immediately and acknowledges the client.
The update cannot propagate. A and B now hold different values for the same key.

B answers the read with stale data rather than an error. Every request gets a response; some responses are out of date. This is what a social feed should do — a slightly stale timeline is fine, an error page is not.
When the partition heals, the divergence has to be reconciled — last-write-wins, vector clocks, or handing both versions to the application. Choosing AP is choosing to handle conflicts.

flows.name: It's per operation, not per database

steps.text: Within one product the answer differs by feature. Adding to a cart should stay available — losing it loses a sale.

Decrementing the last unit of inventory should favour consistency — overselling costs money and trust. Same system, opposite choices, and saying that is what shows you understand the theorem rather than reciting it.
